title: Diwali 2026 greeting: one lamp lights the next

lines.say: Diwali comes on the darkest night of the month.
lines.show: Diwali comes on the darkest night of the month.

lines.say: We draw a rangoli at the door, and light one lamp.
lines.show: We draw a rangoli at the door, and light one lamp.

lines.say: Then the next one, from the first.
lines.show: Then the next one, from the first.

lines.say: A flame gives its light, and loses nothing.
lines.show: A flame gives its light, and loses nothing.

lines.say: Happy Diwali, from all of us at Your Rider.
lines.show: Happy Diwali, from all of us at Yourider.

on_screen.end_sign: from all of us at Yourider

sfx.note: tanpura-like drone; gain 0.18 keeps it >=10 dB under the voice (QA 2026-11-04)
one small bell on the greeting

_voice_free_beat: 14.4-15.4 s: no voice; the drone and flames continue (a dead-silent gap would fail check.py's dead-air check and break the warmth)
sfx_dir: media/.build/diwali-2026/sfx (made by sounds.py, synthesised, see rights.md)

lamp_carry._note: seconds the spark takes from lamp n-1's flame to lamp n's wick; it leaves at (lamp n ignition - carry). Ignition times are the catch cues above (sfx[].lamp), read by gen.py, so sound and picture share one source.
